This figure is from AC 43.13-1B, Acceptable Methods, Techniques, and Practices: Aircraft Inspection and Repair, chapter 7 (aircraft hardware, control cables, and turnbuckles). Its caption: "FIGURE 7-2. Torque wrench with various adapters.".
Describe it for a mechanic who can't see it: say what it shows, then transcribe every label,
value, unit, part number, and note printed in it. Don't add anything that isn't in the figure.
If it shows nothing of use (a logo, a signature, a blank area), say so in one sentence.

message.content:
The figure shows torque wrench adapters and formulas for calculating corrected torque readings when using adapters that change the distance from the torque wrench drive to the adapter drive.

NOTE
WHEN USING A TORQUE WRENCH ADAPTER WHICH CHANGES THE DISTANCE FROM THE TORQUE WRENCH DRIVE TO THE ADAPTER DRIVE, APPLY THE FOLLOWING FORMULAS TO OBTAIN THE CORRECTED TORQUE READING:

Short Open End Adapter
Set Screw Adapter
Hose Clamp Adapter

ADAPTER DRIVE CENTERLINE
TORQUE WRENCH
WRENCH DRIVE CENTERLINE
HANDGRIP CENTERLINE (PREDETERMINED)
E
L

FORMULA T×L / L-E = Y

EXAMPLE: (WITH "E" AS PLUS DIMENSION)
T = 135 LB. IN.
Y = UNKNOWN
L = 10.0 IN.
E = 1.5 IN.

Y = 135 × 10 / 10 + 1.5 = 1350 / 11.5 = 117.39
Y = 117 LB. IN.

LEGEND
T = ACTUAL (DESIRED) TORQUE
Y = APPARENT (INDICATED) TORQUE
L = EFFECTIVE LENGTH LEVER
E = EFFECTIVE LENGTH OF EXTENSION

Open-End Wrench Adapter
Flare Nut Wrench Adapter
Spanner Wrench Adapter

TORQUE WRENCH
WRENCH DRIVE CENTERLINE
ADAPTER DRIVE CENTERLINE
HANDGRIP CENTERLINE (PREDETERMINED)
E
L

FORMULA T×L / L-E = Y

EXAMPLE: (WITH "E" AS MINUS DIMENSION)
T = 135 LB. IN.
Y = UNKNOWN
L = 10.0 IN.
E = 1.5 IN.

Y = 135 × 10 / 10 - 1.5 = 1350 / 8.5 = 158.82
Y = 159 LB. IN.
